title: Road to bigger shoulders update
summary: A short shoulder update: he deliberately keeps his delts smaller than his arms but wants round, capped 3D delts, built mainly through lateral and rear delt work. He shows how lats push the delts out for a rounder look and says pressing strength matters less than delt size because of leverages.
claims: For his goal physique he keeps his delts relatively small on purpose; biceps and triceps must always look bigger than the delts
Round, capped 3D delts are achievable naturally by focusing on the lateral and rear delts, since the front delt is usually overdeveloped from pressing
The side delt is the portion lacking in most people and should be built with lateral raises and specialized exercises
Well-developed lats let you push the delts outward when flexing, creating an illusion of roundness that disappears when relaxed
Overhead pressing is a must, but pressing strength is largely irrelevant: poor leverages mean you need bigger delts to lift less, so judge by shoulder size, not load
His plan is to keep throwing tonnage at the shoulders and expects more definition, vascularity and roundness rather than major size
exercises: build the side delt, which is lacking in most people
a must for shoulders, but leverage dictates load more than size
stats: capped, vascular, kept smaller than arms
